title: Learn Vietnamese in Ho Chi Minh City and find your people
description: Where to study Vietnamese in Saigon, southern vs northern speech, phrases for class and the staff room, and how teachers make friends and handle loneliness.
h1: Learning Vietnamese in Ho Chi Minh City and building a life outside the classroom
intro: For classes in Ho Chi Minh City, two long-running schools teach Vietnamese to foreigners: the university Center for Vietnamese Language and Culture (VLC) and the private Vietnamese Language Studies (VLS), with offices in the centre, Thao Dien and Phu My Hung. Neither lists fees or start dates on its main pages, so ask by email. Learn the southern speech you hear every day, keep a dozen everyday phrases ready, and build your social life around weekday daytime: centre teaching takes your evenings and weekends.
keyPoints: **Two long-running schools**: the university centre (VLC, 10–12 Dinh Tien Hoang) and the private VLS, which teaches in person and online from offices in the centre, Thao Dien and Phu My Hung. Neither lists prices or start dates on its main pages, so ask for both in writing.

**Learn southern Vietnamese if you live in Saigon.** Northerners and southerners understand each other, but many courses and textbooks use Hanoi pronunciation, and in everyday southern speech two of the six tones sound alike. Ask which accent a course uses.
**Vietnamese is for the edges of a lesson**: greetings, praise, safety and the staff room. Agree with your teaching assistant when Vietnamese is acceptable in class.
**Your hours run against the city's social life.** Centre classes are mostly weekday evenings and all day at weekends, so plan study, sport and friendships for weekday mornings.
**Tet 2027 falls on 6 February.** Centres close, much of the city goes home to family and the first Tet alone hits many newcomers hardest, so make a plan in advance.

sections.title: Where to learn Vietnamese in Ho Chi Minh City

blocks.text: Two long-running schools teach Vietnamese to foreigners in the city. The university route is the [Center for Vietnamese Language and Culture (VLC)](https://vlc.hcmussh.edu.vn/index.php/introduction/) at the University of Social Sciences and Humanities, Vietnam National University HCMC. It was formally set up in 2020 under a Vietnamese Studies faculty that says it has taught Vietnamese to foreigners for more than 34 years. Besides courses, it runs study tours, Vietnamese proficiency tests and training for teachers of Vietnamese.

The main private option is [Vietnamese Language Studies (VLS)](https://vlstudies.com/), operating since about 1994. It teaches in person and online from beginner to advanced, with courses including Survival Vietnamese, Pronunciation, Business Vietnamese and Culture & Mentality, plus corporate classes. Its three offices are close to where many teachers live, which matters when you study between classes.

blocks.text: Old district names are still how people, signs and Grab drivers describe the city, but since 1 July 2025 [official addresses use new ward names](https://baodauthau.vn/tphcm-co-113-phuong-54-xa-va-1-dac-khu-sau-sap-xep-post180312.html): the old District 1 core is mainly Sai Gon and Ben Thanh wards, Thao Dien is in An Khanh ward, and Phu My Hung is mainly Tan My and Tan Hung. If you have not chosen a home yet, a school near it saves real time; see [where teachers live in the city](/teach-in-vietnam/where-to-live-in-ho-chi-minh-city-as-a-teacher).

Before you pay anywhere, ask four things by email: the fee and what it covers, the next start date, how many hours a week, and **which accent the course teaches**. Many teachers also take a private tutor once the first course ends; rates and quality vary, so book a single trial lesson first.

sections.title: A study plan that fits a teacher's timetable

blocks.text: Language-centre work is concentrated in the hours other people are free. The chain VUS says [most of its classes are on weekday evenings and all day at weekends](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979), mostly for 6–16-year-olds. That leaves weekday mornings and early afternoons for study, which is when schools and tutors are easiest to book.

items.title: Take a short survival course in your first two months
items.text: A common pattern among teachers is a 4–6 week course covering numbers, tones, ordering food and giving directions. It pays for itself in fewer misunderstandings at the market, with landlords and on Grab.

items.title: Get the tones right early, with a human ear
items.text: Vietnamese uses tone to tell words apart: ma, má, mà, mả, mã and mạ are six different words. An app can drill vocabulary, but a teacher or tutor has to hear you say them and correct you before bad habits set in.

items.title: Add a weekly tutor or a language exchange
items.text: After the course, an hour a week with a tutor keeps you moving. A language exchange (your English for their Vietnamese) is free and doubles as a way to meet people, but agree at the start how the time is split.

items.title: Use it every day where the stakes are low
items.text: Order food, read prices, give your address to drivers and greet the guard at your building in Vietnamese. Ask Vietnamese colleagues to correct you; many are glad to.

blocks.text: Learning some Vietnamese also makes you a better English teacher. You will start to hear why your students drop final sounds and struggle with particular consonants, which our guide to [pronunciation problems of Vietnamese learners](/teach-in-vietnam/pronunciation-problems-of-vietnamese-learners) explains.

sections.title: Southern or northern Vietnamese: which should you learn?

blocks.text: Vietnamese is one language with clear regional accents and some regional words. Northerners and southerners understand each other without trouble, and nothing you learn in one accent is wasted. But many courses and textbooks use northern (Hanoi) pronunciation, and a beginner trained only on northern sounds can find Saigon speech hard to follow at first.

If you live and work in Saigon, the practical choice is **southern pronunciation and vocabulary**, because that is what your colleagues, students' parents, landlord and drivers speak. The main differences a learner notices:

items: **Tones**: northern speech keeps six distinct tones. In everyday southern speech the hỏi and ngã tones sound the same, so you hear five.
**Some consonants**: d and gi sound like English "z" in the north and like "y" in the south; v often sounds like "y" in southern speech.
**Word endings**: in the south, final n and ng, and final t and c, often sound alike.
**Everyday words**: a handful of common words differ, several of them on menus (table below).

blocks.caption: Common everyday words that differ between Saigon and Hanoi Vietnamese
rows: bệnh (ốm means thin in the south)

blocks.text: If you might move north later, the switch is manageable once you have the basics. The wider city choice is covered in [Hanoi vs Ho Chi Minh City for teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/hanoi-vs-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers).

sections.title: Vietnamese phrases for the classroom and the staff room

blocks.text: Centres hire you to teach in English, so Vietnamese belongs at the edges of a lesson, not in the middle of it. A useful habit is to agree with your Vietnamese teaching assistant before class when Vietnamese is acceptable, typically for very young children, safety, complicated instructions and behaviour, and to keep behaviour management a shared job. More on working with assistants is in [Vietnamese classroom culture for English teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnamese-classroom-culture-for-english-teachers).

Address matters as much as vocabulary. Teachers have high status in Vietnam, captured in the proverb ["Không thầy đố mày làm nên"](https://fass.nus.edu.sg/cls/wp-content/uploads/sites/32/2020/10/pham_thimyhanh.pdf) (without a teacher you cannot succeed). Students, and often parents and staff, will call you **thầy** (male teacher) or **cô** (female teacher), usually followed by your first name. You call students **em**, and adult colleagues **anh** (a man) or **chị** (a woman) if they are older than you or about your age. Adding **ạ** at the end of a sentence makes it more polite.

sections.title: How teachers meet people in Saigon

blocks.text: Most teachers' first friends are colleagues: the other foreign teachers on the same evening shifts and the Vietnamese staff who sort out your timetable. Beyond work, the established routes are expat and teacher groups online, structured clubs, sport and study. Club schedules change often, so treat the details below as leads to check, not fixed facts.

blocks.text: Your Vietnamese class is itself a social network: classmates are usually other newcomers with the same free hours. Language exchanges work the same way and also bring you Vietnamese friends, the people who can explain the city from the inside. Sport clubs, gyms and running groups mostly organise through social media; go twice before you judge one.

Online groups are useful, but they are also where fake job offers circulate. The UK government's [travel advice for Vietnam](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/vietnam/safety-and-security) warns that offers that look too good to be true have ended in trafficking to neighbouring countries to work in online scams. Check any offer that comes through a group the way our guide to [teaching job scams in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam) sets out.
Volunteering

Volunteering is a good way to meet people, but be careful when it means teaching. Unpaid teaching is not automatically outside the work-permit rules: the volunteer exemption in [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html) covers unpaid work that carries out an international treaty Vietnam has joined, confirmed by a foreign embassy or an international organisation. Working without a required permit is fined {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} with possible deportation under [Decree 283/2026/ND-CP](https://suckhoedoisong.vn/tu-10-9-2026-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-se-bi-phat-neu-khong-co-giay-phep-lao-dong-169260824224738.htm), in force since 10 September 2026. Before you volunteer in a classroom, ask the organisation in writing whether it needs a permit or exemption for you; [the work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) explains how permits work. Non-teaching help, such as events or fundraising, avoids the question.

blocks.title: Nights out and house parties
blocks.text: The UK travel advice warns of drink spiking and of methanol-laced alcohol, including drinks bought in licensed bars, shops and hotels. It also says police raid nightlife venues and, when responding to a reported disturbance, **routinely drug-test people at private homes and parties**. A positive test can lead to prosecution. Buy your own drinks, keep them in sight, stick to sealed bottles or known brands, and do not assume a house party is a safe place to break the law.

sections.title: Loneliness and culture shock: what to expect

blocks.text: Many people who move abroad find the novelty carries them through the first weeks and the dip comes a few months in, once paperwork is done and routine sets in. For teachers in Saigon four things make it sharper, and all four can be planned for.

items: **The timetable.** Evening and weekend teaching means your free time is when most friends are at work. Read [how workloads and schedules run](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-workload-and-schedules-in-vietnam) before you sign, and protect one weekend block a month if your contract allows it.

**Tet.** Tet 2027 falls on Saturday 6 February, with the [public-sector break from 4 to 10 February](https://suckhoedoisong.vn/chinh-thuc-tet-nguyen-dan-2027-nghi-7-ngay-quoc-khanh-nghi-4-ngay-169261002184541968.htm). Centres and many schools close for a week or more, small eateries and shops shut for days and colleagues go home to family. Travel, accept if a colleague invites you to their family's celebration, or plan something with other newcomers; just do not let it arrive unplanned.

**The classroom.** Vietnamese students often [stay quiet and wait to be called on](https://fass.nus.edu.sg/cls/wp-content/uploads/sites/32/2020/10/pham_thimyhanh.pdf) as a mark of respect, and face-saving matters to them and their families. New teachers often read that silence as rejection; it usually is not.
**Daily life.** Heat, traffic, noise and the rainy season wear people down at first; a routine and a reliable way to get around take much of the strain out.

blocks.text: What helps is unglamorous: a fixed weekly commitment outside work (a class, a club, a sport), at least one Vietnamese friend or tutor you see regularly, a daytime routine that gets you out of the flat, and staying in touch with home without living on its time zone.

sections.title: When it is more than homesickness

blocks.text: If low mood, anxiety or drinking start to take over, get professional help early. Family Medical Practice's clinic at 95 Thao Dien, An Khanh ward, is open 24/7 and [lists psychiatry among its services](https://www.vietnammedicalpractice.com/locations/ho-chi-minh/); its emergency line is *9999 or 028 3744 9000. Some people keep seeing a therapist from home by video, which is worth arranging before you fly.

In an emergency, call 115 for an ambulance or 113 for the police; [112 is a separate line for disasters and search-and-rescue](https://en.mae.gov.vn/hotline-112-to-receive-disaster-and-emergency-reports-nationwide-9018.htm). English support on public lines is limited, so save a private hospital's emergency number as well. What national and private health insurance cover is set out in [healthcare and health insurance in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/healthcare-and-health-insurance-in-ho-chi-minh-city).

faqs.q: How much do Vietnamese classes cost in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Neither the university centre (VLC) nor Vietnamese Language Studies publishes fees or start dates on the pages checked in October 2026. Email both, ask what the fee includes and how many hours a week the course runs, and compare the replies.

faqs.q: Is it worth learning Hanoi Vietnamese if I live in Saigon?
faqs.a: It is not wasted, because northern and southern speakers understand each other. But southern pronunciation and words are what you hear every day in Saigon, so a course in the southern accent gets you understanding people around you sooner.

faqs.q: Do I need to speak Vietnamese to teach English in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Centres hire foreign teachers to teach in English, and a Vietnamese teaching assistant usually handles anything that needs Vietnamese. A few phrases still help with very young learners, safety and colleagues.

faqs.q: Can I volunteer as an English teacher instead of working?
faqs.a: Be careful. Vietnam's volunteer exemption from the work permit is narrow (unpaid work under an international treaty, confirmed by an embassy or international organisation), and working without a required permit can mean a fine and deportation. Ask the organisation in writing whether it needs a permit or exemption for you before you start.
